x: God Almighty says, And the winds that scatter the dust. He says, And the winds that scatter the dust. It is said, The wind scatter the dust. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, he said:
m: A man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: What is Adh-Dhariyat? He said: It is the wind.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, he said:
m: I heard Khalid bin Arʿarah say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, go out to the square wearing two cloaks, and they said: If a man asked and the people heard, he said: So Ibn Al-Kawwa stood up and said: What is Adh-Dhariyat? He said: It is the wind.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd al-Hilali and Muhammad ibn Bashar told me, they said: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthma told us, he said: Musa ibn Yaqub al-Zumai told us, he said: Abu al-Huwayrith told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im,
m: he told him, he said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, addressing the people, and Abdullah ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted, And the winds that scatter scatter. They are the winds.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, he said:
m: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, was asked about the winds that scatter. He said: The wind.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Ali:
m: And the winds that scatter he said: the wind. Mahran said: He told us on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Ar’ah, who said: I asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about the winds that scatter. He said: It is the wind.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Abi Bazza, who said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Tayyib say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: Do not ask me about a speaking book or a past Sunnah except that I will tell you. So Ibn Al-Kawwa asked him about Al-Dhariyat, and he said: They are the winds.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Talq told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ali bin Rabi’ah, who said:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa’ asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he said: And the winds that scatter. He said: It is the wind.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, he said:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa’ said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: What is the wind? He said: The wind.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yahya bin Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Sakhra, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu al-Sahbaa al-Bakri, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, he said, while he was on the pulpit, No one asks me about a verse from the Book of God except that I inform him. So Ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up and wanted to ask him about what Subaygh had asked Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, so he said, What are the winds that scatter? Ali said, The winds.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: that a man asked Ali about the winds. He said: They are the winds.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Wahb ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, he said:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali, saying: What is the wind that scatters? He said: The winds.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the scatterers
, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say that they are the winds.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the scatterers
, he said: The winds.

x: And his saying, And those that carry loads, means: The clouds that carry their load of water.
And his saying, And the ships that sail smoothly means: The ships that sail smoothly in the seas

And the angels who divide the matter He says: The angels who divide the matter of God among His creation And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Hannad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, who said:
m: A man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: What are the ones that sail smoothly? He said: They are the ships. He said: What are the ones that carry a load? He said: They are the clouds. He said: What are the ones that divide a matter? He said: They are the angels.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, who said:
m: I heard Khalid bin Arʿarah say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: What are the carriers of burdens? He said: They are the clouds. He said: What are the ones that run smoothly? He said: They are the ships. He said: What are the ones who divide a matter? He said: They are the angels.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali,
m: in a similar manner.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd al-Hilali and Muhammad ibn Bashar told me: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthma told us: Musa al-Zumai told us: Abu al-Huwayrith told me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im who told him:
m: I heard Ali addressing the people, and Ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted: And those carrying loads He said: They are the clouds. And those running with ease He said: They are the ships. And those distributing a matter He said: The angels.
b.via: on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im who

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Abi Bazza:
m: I heard Abu Al-Tayyib say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, who said:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa’ said to Ali, and he mentioned something similar to it: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Wahb ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, who said: I witnessed Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up to him and mentioned something similar.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Talq bin Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ali bin Rabi’ah, who said:
m: I asked Ibn al-Kawwa’ about Ali, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu al-Sahbaa al-Bakri, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, something similar.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: that a man asked Ali and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Ali,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, who said:
m: He was asked and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And those carrying burdens, he said: The clouds. His statement, And those who divide a matter, he said: The angels.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And those carrying loads He said: The clouds carrying rain. And those running smoothly He said: The ships. And those distributing a command He said: The angels, He sends them down by His command to whomever He wills.

x: His statement, Indeed, what you are promised is true. God Almighty says, Indeed, what you are promised, O people, of the establishment of the Hour and the resurrection of the dead from their graves is true. He says, It is a true and certain thing that will happen. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
You are only promised to one who is truthful
. The meaning is: to be truthful, so the noun was placed in place of the source.

x: And the religion is certain He says: And the clouds, reward, and punishment are certain, and God will reward His servants according to their deeds. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And indeed, the judgment will come to pass, he said: The reckoning.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “What you are promised is true. And indeed, the judgment will come to pass.” That is on the Day of Resurrection, the day on which people will be judged by their deeds.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, the judgment will come to pass. He said: On the day when God will judge the servants according to their deeds.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, And indeed, the religion will surely come to pass, he said, It will come to pass.

x: God Almighty says: And the sky of beautiful creation. And by His saying of interweaving He meant of the paths and the breaking of everything is habaka and it is the plural of habaka and habika. It is said of the breaking of curly hair habaka and of the sand when the still wind passes over it and the standing water and the iron armor has habaka and from this the rajaz poet says. As if the weaver had covered her with a rug, and woven it with silk I went to the heartbeat and the mind And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, although the words of those who said it differed.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me: Abthar told us: Hasin told us on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And the sky with its woven paths, he said: with its beautiful creation.
b.via: Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the sky with its constellations. He said: Its beauty and its evenness.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And the sky with its intertwined spaces. He said: Its intertwining spaces are its beauty and its evenness. He said: Hakam told us:

c: Amr told us, on the authority of Omar bin Saeed bin Masrouq,
m: the brother of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And the sky with its ornaments, he said: with its adornments.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told us: Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement, And the sky with its intricate patterns, he said, It was intricately woven with beautiful patterns, it was intricately woven with stars.

c: Ibn Bashar told me: Hudha told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement, And the sky of interwoven spaces, he said: It was interwoven with beautiful creation, it was interwoven with stars.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Uthman bin Al-Haitham told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement, And the sky with its interwoven spaces, he said: It has beautiful creations interwoven with stars.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Imran bin Hudayr told us:
m: Ikrimah was asked about His statement, And the heaven of interwoven fabrics. He said: Of beautiful creation. Have you not seen a weaver when he weaves a garment and says: How beautifully he interwoven it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qurbah, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Behind you is the liar and the misleader, and behind his head is a braid, a braid, meaning the curly braid.
b.via: a man from the companions of the Prophet

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the sky with its constellations. He said: Its smoothness is its beauty. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Ali bin Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, And the sky with its woven patterns, meaning the one with the good character. He said: Thabit Mahran, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Its stars intertwine with it. Ibn Abbas used to say: Intertwined means the one with beautiful features.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying, And the sky with its stars, meaning with its beautiful creation. Al-Hasan used to say, Its stars are its stars.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The one with the beautiful character means the one with the beautiful character.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the sky of interconnected spaces, he said: The well-constructed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the sky full of ornaments, meaning full of adornments. It is also said that its ornaments are like the ornamentation of sand, like the ornamentation of armor, and like the ornamentation of water when you strike it and weave it into paths.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, of the interlocking, he said:

x: And His statement, Indeed, you are in a different statement, means: You, O people, are in a different statement regarding this Qur’an. Some believe in it and some deny it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: You are in a different statement. He said: Some believe in this Qur’an and some deny it.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, Indeed, you are in a different statement, he said: They are guessing, saying, This is magic, and they are saying, This is myths, so which of their statements should be taken? The guessers killed this man. He must have one of these in him. So why do you not take one of these, when you have accused him of various statements? So which of these statements should you take? It is a different statement. He said: Then he mentioned that it was their guessing, and they had no knowledge of that. They said: So what prevented this Qur’an from being revealed in the language in which the books before you were revealed? So God said, A foreigner and an Arab. If We had made this Qur’an a foreigner, you would have said, We are Arabs, and this Qur’an is a foreigner. So how can they come together?

x: And his saying, Whoever turns away from it will be turned away from it, means: Whoever turns away from it will be turned away from believing in this Qur’an, and whoever turns away from it will be pushed away and deprived of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Whoever is slandered will be punished. He said: Ibn Amr said in his hadith, He will be paid back or He will be punished or a word similar to it. Al-Harith said, He will be punished without a doubt.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: He who turns away from him will be turned away. He said: He who turns away will be turned away from him.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: He who is lied to will be lied to. So what is lied to today means the Book of God.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, He who is turned away from it is turned away,: The polytheists are turned away from it.

x: God Almighty says: He cursed the fortune-tellers who conjecture lies and falsehood and assume them to be true. The commentators differed about who was meant by his statement, killing the liars.
Some of them said that it meant the doubters.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The liars were killed
, meaning: The doubters were cursed.

x: Others said the same thing we said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, The charlatans were killed, he said: The soothsayers.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
The liars were killed
. He said: Those who fabricate lies, as He said in Abasa 80:The man was killed.

c: Abasa 17 And each of them told me
m: with the chain of transmission that I mentioned from him on the authority of Mujahid:
h
The liars were killed
. He said: Those who say: We will not be resurrected, and they do not have certainty.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The liars killed means the people of suspicion.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
The liars were killed
, that they are the people who fabricate lies about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: A group said, He is only a magician and the one who brought it is magic.
A group said, He is only a poet and the one who brought it is poetry.
A group said, He is only a soothsayer and the one who brought it is soothsaying.

A group said, Legends of the ancients which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening. Al-Furqan 25:5 They fabricate lies about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
And His statement,
h
Those who are in a state of heedlessness

, God Almighty says: Those who are in the midst of misguidance and are overcome by it, persisting and neglecting the truth with which God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, although their wording differed in explaining it.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those who are in a state of heedlessness
, meaning: they persist in their misguidance.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those who are in a state of heedlessness
, he said: In heedlessness and inattentive.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Those who are in a state of heedlessness
means:
h
in a state of heedlessness
and doubt.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan,
m: Ghamrat Sahun meaning: in a state of negligence.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
In a state of heedlessness
, he said: Heedless of what came to them, what was sent down to them, and what God Almighty commanded them. And he recited the statement of God, the Most High, Rather, their hearts are
h
in a state of heedlessness
about this, the verse, and he said: Do you not see that when you take something and then immerse it in water?

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In the midst of a heedless person means his heart is in a quiver.

x: And His statement, They ask, ‘
h
When is the Day of Judgment
?’ God Almighty says, these liars, whose characteristics He described, ask when is the Day of Recompense and Reckoning and the Day when God will judge the servants according to their deeds.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
When is the Day of Judgment
? He said, Those who deny that they will be judged or resurrected.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They ask, ‘
h
When is the Day of Judgment
?’ He said: They say,
h
When is the Day of Judgment
? or Will there be a Day of Judgment?

x: And His statement,
h
On the Day when they will be tested in the Fire
, God Almighty says,
h
On the Day when they will be tested in the Fire
of Hell. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement, they will be tested in this context.
Some of them said that it means that they will be tortured by being burned in fire. Mention who said that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day they will be tested over the Fire
, he said, they will be tormented.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, They ask, ‘When is the Day of Judgment?’ The Day they will be tested over the Fire. He said: Their trial is that they asked about the Day of Judgment while they were standing over the Fire. “Taste your trial. This is what you used to hasten.” So they said when they were stood up, Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment. As-Saffat 37:20. And God, glory be to Him, said, This is the Day of Separation which you used to deny. As-Saffat 37:21.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They are tested, he said: Just as gold is tested in the fire.

c: Yaqoub told me: Hisham told me: Hisin told us on the authority of Ikrimah
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire
, he said: They will be tormented in the Fire and burned in it. Have you not seen that when gold is thrown into the Fire, it is said to be tested?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire
, he said: They will be tormented.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: On the Day they will be tested by the Fire, meaning they will be cooked by the Fire.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: On the Day when they will be tested by the Fire, he said: They will be burned.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: On the Day when they will be tested by the Fire, meaning they will be burned.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say about The Day they will be tested by the Fire, that he said: They will be cooked as gold is tested by fire.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire
, he said: They will be burned by the Fire.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
On the Day they will be tested over the Fire
. He said: They will be burned.

x: Others said that he meant that they were lying. Mention who said that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire

, he said: They will be cooked. It is also said: They will be tested means they will lie. All of this is said. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the accusative of the word day in the phrase the day they are tempted by the Fire.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said that it is accusative of time and the meaning in when is the Day of Judgment is when is the Day of Judgment. So it was said to them: in the day they are tempted by the Fire, because that day is a long day in which there is the reckoning and in which they are tempted by the Fire.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said that you put the word the day of them in the accusative case because you added it to two things. If the day and the night are added to a noun that has a verb and they are raised, the day is in the accusative case even if it is in the genitive or nominative case if it is added to a verb or does something, or if it is like that and raising it in the nominative case and lowering it in the genitive case is permissible. So if it was said the day of them upon the fire, they are tempted, raising the day would be appropriate, but none of the reciters recited it that way. Another of them said: It is an accusative of
h
On the Day when they are over the Fire being tested

, the statement of the one who said: They are tormented by burning, because the origin of the word test is choice. Rather, it is said: He tested the gold with fire if you cooked it with it to know its quality.
So too is his statement:
h
On the Day when they are over the Fire being tested
, they are burned with it as gold is burned. As for the accusative of on the Day, it is because it is

evidence.text: So if it was said the day of them upon the fire, they are tempted, raising the day would be appropriate, but none of the reciters recited it that way.

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
Taste your trial
, that they are told,
h
Taste your trial
, and He left out saying,
h
Taste your trial
, because the words indicate it. And by His saying, Your trial, He means your torment and your burning.
The interpreters differed on this, and some of them said what we said about it. Mention who said that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, your trial, he said, your burning.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Taste your trial
. Taste your punishment. This is what you were hastening.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
Taste your trial
, meaning: On the day they are punished, He says, Taste your punishment.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Taste your trial
, meaning your burning.

c: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Taste your trial
, he said: Taste your punishment.

x: Others said about me: Taste your torture or your lies. Mention who said that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, my uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Taste your trial
, meaning your denial.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Taste your trial

, meaning: your burning, and it is said: your lie. And His statement, This is what you were hastening for, God Almighty says, It will be said to them, ‘This punishment that you are being inflicted with today is the punishment that you were hastening for in this world.’

x: And His statement, Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. God Almighty says, Indeed, those who feared God by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience in this world will be among gardens and springs of water in the Hereafter.
And His statement,
h
Taking what their Lord has given them

, God Almighty says, Doing what their Lord has commanded them to do, fulfilling His obligations. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Omar, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
taking what their Lord has given them

, he said: The obligatory duties. His saying, They were, before that, doers of good, means that they were, before the obligations were imposed upon them, doers of good. He says, They were, before that, obedient. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Omar, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Indeed, they were before that doers of good. He said: Before the obligatory duties, they were doers of good deeds.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of his statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
Some of them said that it means they did not sleep but little of the night. They said that what means denial. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed and Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik:
m: They used to sleep little at night. He said: They would stay awake and pray between these two prayers, between sunset and evening prayers.

c: Zurayq bin Al-Shahab told me: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us, Bakir bin Abi Al-Samat told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, he said: They would not sleep until they had prayed the Isha prayer. They said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us:

c: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mutraf,
m: regarding His statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
, he said: Not a single night passed them by without them praying.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: who said: Mutraf bin Abdullah said regarding His statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, “Say, a night will come upon them in which they do not pray to God, either from the beginning of it or from the middle of it.”

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Ibn Abi Layla told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
They used to sleep but little of the night

. He said: Not a night would pass without them taking at least a little of it. He said: Ibn Yaman told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah who said: They used to make mistakes in it.

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me: Hafs bin Asim told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, he said: They did not sleep between sunset and evening prayers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam and Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: They used to sleep little at night. He said: They used to make mistakes at night.
b.via: Abu Jaʿfar on the authority of al-Rabiʿ

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba on the authority of Mutraf
m: regarding his statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, he said: Say, A night came upon them and they slept all of it.
b.via: Saeed bin Abi Aruba on the authority of Mutraf

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They used to sleep but little of the night
. He said:
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, and they used to pray it.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us:
m: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say about His statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
, that they slept little at night until morning.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
, he said: They slept little at night until morning, without praying at night.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they slept a little at night, and they explained the ma in his statement they slept to be a connection. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
. He said: Al-Hasan said, They struggled to perform the night prayers.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: They do not sleep except a little of it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of some of our companions on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement,
h
They used to sleep but little of the night
, he said: They did not sleep at night except for a little of it.
b.via: some of our companions on the authority of Al-Hasan

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Wahhab told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
. He said: Say, A night came upon them in which they slept.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Al-Ahnaf bin Qais said
m: regarding His statement,
h
They slept but little of the night
, he said: They did not sleep except a little. And His saying,
h
And in the hours of the pre-dawn hours they seek forgiveness
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is, and in the hours of the pre-dawn hours they pray.God Mention who said that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And in the hours of early morning they seek forgiveness

, meaning they stand and pray. He said: They used to stand and sleep, as God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it, so this is sleep and this is standing, and a group of those with you Al-Muzzammil 20. Likewise, they stand for a third and a half and two-thirds: He said, they sleep and stand.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jablah ibn Suhaim, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And in the hours of dawn they seek forgiveness
, he said: They pray.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And in the hours of dawn they seek forgiveness
. He said: They pray.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was that they delayed seeking forgiveness for their sins until dawn. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: They prolonged the prayer and were energetic until the time for seeking forgiveness was at dawn.

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And in the hours of dawn they seek forgiveness

, he said: They are the believers. He said: It has reached us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Jacob, asked him to seek forgiveness for them, They said, ‘O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins.’ Yusuf 97 He said, ‘I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.’ Yusuf 98 He said: Some of the people of knowledge said: He delayed seeking forgiveness until the early hours of the morning. He said: Some of the people of knowledge mentioned that the hour in which the gates of Paradise are opened is the early hours of the morning.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say: The last sixth of the night is the pre-dawn hours.

x: And His statement,
h
And in their wealth there is a right for the needy and the deprived

, God Almighty says: And in the wealth of these good people whose characteristics He described there is a right for the needy who asks from them and the deprived. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of the questioner, the people of interpretation said, and they differed about the meaning of the deprived.
Some said: He is the one who has no share in Islam. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
m: I asked him about the beggar and the deprived. He said: The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam and is a heretic.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And in their wealth is a right for the needy and the deprived
. He said: The deprived are the ones who are deprived.

c: Sahl bin Musa Al-Razi told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The beggar is the beggar, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam.

c: Sahl bin Musa told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The deprived one is the one who has no share in Islam.

c: Hamid bin Masʿadah told us: Yazid bin Zariʿ told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
For the beggar and the deprived
. The beggar said: The one who asks, and the deprived is the one who is deprived.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us:
m: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating on the authority of Qais Ibn Karkam on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: The deprived, he said: The deprived.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and the deprived, that he is the deprived man who has no money except that it is gone, and God has decreed that for him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais ibn Karkam, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement,
h
For the beggar and the deprived
. He said: The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who has been deviated from the path and has no share in Islam.

c: Muhammad bin Amr Al-Muqaddami told me: Quraysh bin Anas told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said
m: about the deprived: He is the one who is deprived and has no one to take care of him or give him anything.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Wahb bin Jarir told me: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said:
m: A flood came to Al-Yamamah and took away the wealth of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: This is the deprived one.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us on the authority of Nafi’
m: who said: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Muslim bin Khalid told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted.

x: God Almighty says: And on the earth are lessons and admonitions for those who are certain of the truth of what they have witnessed and seen when they wander about in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And on the earth are signs for those of certainty
, he said: He says: A lesson for those who take lesson.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And on the earth are signs for those of certainty
, if he travels on the earth of God, he will see great lessons and signs.

x: And His statement,
h
And in yourselves
, so will you not see?
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And in the path of defecation and urination in yourselves is a lesson for you and a proof for you about your Lord. So will you not see that from you?God Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Samad Al-Ansari told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Al-Murtafi’, who said:
m: I heard Ibn Al-Zubayr say:
h
And in yourselves
, so will you not see? He said: The path of defecation and urination.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And in yourselves
. Will you not see?” He said: The path of defecation and urination.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: In God Almighty’s arrangement of the joints of your bodies and limbs, there is evidence for you that you were created to worship Him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And in yourselves

, then will you not see? And he recited the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted, And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly, you are human beings dispersing. Ar-Rum 20 He said: And among us are many signs: this hearing, this sight, this tongue, and this heart. No one knows what is black or red, and this speech that he stutters with, and this heart, what it is, is only a morsel in his stomach in which God places the mind. Does anyone know what that mind is, what its description is, and what it is like? The correct thing to say about this is to say: The meaning of this is:
h
And in yourselves

also, O people, are signs and lessons that guide you to the oneness of your Creator and that you have no god other than Him, since nothing is able to create like His creation of you. Do you not see? He says: Do you not look at this and reflect on it and learn the truth of the oneness of your Creator?

x: And His statement,
h
And in the sky is your provision
, God Almighty says: And in the sky is the rain and snow through which the earth produces your provision and sustenance of food, fruits, and other things.
Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Mention who said that.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Al-Nadr told us: Juwaybir told us on the authority of Ad-Dahhak
m: regarding his statement,
h
And in the sky is your provision
, he said: Rain.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’at, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And in the sky is your provision and that which you are promised
, he said: Snow and every melting spring of snow that does not decrease.

c: Yunus bin Ubaj Al-A’la told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: In the clouds is your provision, by God, but you deprive yourself of it because of your sins and deeds. He said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, who said: I think it was him or someone else, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man saying: And it rained on us because of some of the lion’s cubs. He said: You have lied, rather it is God’s provision.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And in the sky is your provision and that which you are promised
. He said: Your provision is rain. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan,
h
And in the sky is your provision
. He said: Your provision is rain.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that your provision is from God who is in the heavens. And who interpreted it as such? The origin of Al-Ahdab.

c: Ibn Hamid told us:
m: Harun bin Al-Mughira, one of the people of opinion, told us on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, who said: Wasil Al-Ahadab recited this verse: And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised, and he said: Behold, my provision is in the heaven and I seek it on the earth. So he entered a ruin and remained there for three days without obtaining anything. Then, on the third day, he saw a date palm grove. He had a brother who was better-intentioned than him, so he entered with him and they became two palm groves. This remained their habit until death separated them. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement,
h
And what you are promised

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is:
h
And what you are promised
of good or evil.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And what you are promised
. He said:
h
And what you are promised
of good or evil.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised. He says: Paradise is in the heaven and that which you are promised of good or evil.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
And what you are promised
of Paradise and Hell. Mention who said that.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Al-Nadr told us: Juwaybir told us on the authority of Ad-Dahhak
m: regarding his statement,
h
And what you are promised
, he said: Paradise and Hell.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And what you are promised
of Paradise. The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion said by Mujahid, because God made the report general with His saying,
h
and what you are promised
, regarding everything that He promised us of good or evil, and He did not specify some over others, so it is general, just as God, may His praise be glorified, made it general.

evidence.text: Ibn Hamid told us: Harun bin Al-Mughira, one of the people of opinion, told us on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, who said: Wasil Al-Ahadab recited this verse: And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised, and he said: Behold, my provision is in the heaven and I seek it on the earth.

x: God Almighty says, swearing to His creation by Himself:
h
By the Lord of the heaven and the earth
, what I have said to you, O people, that in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised is true, just as it is true that you speak.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Khawf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
By the Lord of the heaven and the earth

, it is the truth, just as you speak, he said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, May God curse a people to whom their Lord swore by Himself, but they did not believe Him. Al-Farra’ said: There are two aspects to the combination of ma and in in this context: One of them is that it is similar to the Arabs combining two things from the nouns and tools, as the poet says about the nouns: From the people who, when they fear the mean, knock on the door So he combined allai and alladhi and one of them is sufficient for the other, and as the other said about the tools: I have never seen or heard of anything like this before. So he combined ma and in and they are two denials, one of which is sufficient for the other. As for the other, it is: If that was separated by ma, it would be report that it is true, not a lie. But that is not the meaning of it. Rather, what is meant by it is: It is true, just as it is true that man speaks. Do you not see that your saying: Is your dot more true means: Is it true or a lie? And your saying Is it more true that you speak means for confirmation, not for anything else. So he introduced in to differentiate between the two meanings. He said: So this is the more pleasing of the two meanings to me. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
h
Like what you are

. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as like what in the accusative case, meaning: it has certainly come true, as if they had directed it to the method of the source. It may be permissible for it to be in the accusative case because the Arabs make it in the accusative case with the noun, so they say: like someone who is worshipped, and worshipped God is like you, and you are like him and like him, in the nominative and accusative cases. It may be permissible for it to be in the accusative case according to the method of the source, it has come true like your pronunciation. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Basra recited it as in the nominative case,
h
like what you are

, as an adjective for the truth. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are common in the readings of the regions, but they have similar meanings. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, Like what you are.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as like what in the accusative case, meaning: it has certainly come true, as if they had directed it to the method of the source.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Basra recited it as in the nominative case, like what you are, as an adjective for the truth.
The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are common in the readings of the regions, but they have similar meanings.

the honored guests of Abraham
, the friend of the Most Merciful?
He means by his saying the honored ones as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The honored guests of Abraham
, he said: Abraham honored them and ordered his family to bring them the calf at that time.

x: And his saying, When they entered upon him, means: When Abraham’s guest entered upon him and they said to him, “Peace,” meaning, they submitted completely, he said, “Peace.” The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as Salam said with an alif, meaning he said: Ibrahim has peace upon them. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Salam without an alif, meaning he said: You are peace. And his saying,
h
A people who are unknown
, means: A people whom we do not know. And he raised
h
a people who are unknown
by implying you.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as Salam said with an alif, meaning he said: Ibrahim has peace upon them.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Salam without an alif, meaning he said: You are peace.

x: And his saying,
h
He returned to his family

, means: He turned back to his family and returned. Al-Farra' used to say: Even if the meaning is like this, it is not spoken until its owner has gone or come. He said: Do you not see that you say, The people of Mecca have gone back, and you mean, They returned, or They set out. So if he had concealed his return, it would have been better for him to say, He went back, and He goes back. His saying,
h
So he brought a fat calf
, means: So his guest brought a fat calf that he had cooked until tender.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He returned to his family and brought a fattened calf
. He said: Most of the wealth of the Prophet of God, Abraham, peace be upon him, was cows.

x: And his saying: "
h
So he brought it near to them
. He said: Will you not eat?" And in the speech there is an omitted word, and it is sufficient to indicate what is apparent from it, which is:
h
So he brought it near to them

, so they refrained from eating it, so he said: Will you not eat? So he felt a fear from them, meaning: So Abraham felt in himself fear from his guest and concealed it. "They said: Do not fear, and give him good tidings of a learned boy," meaning: Isaac. And Al-Farra' said: Learned means knowledgeable when he grows up. And Al-Farra' mentioned that some of the elders used to say: If knowledge is awaited, it is said: He is knowledgeable soon and at the end. And in Al-Sayyid Sa'id and Al-Karim Karim, and the one who said Hasan said: This is also good Arabic speech that God said about Al-Alim, Al-Hakim, and the dead.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding his statement, a knowledgeable young man, that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a learned boy, he said: Ishmael. I only said: He meant Isaac because the good report of the child was from Sarah and Ishmael to Hagar, not to Sarah.

x: "So he felt fear of them. They said, 'Do not fear,' and give him good tidings of a learned boy."
His saying,
h
So his wife came in a shriek

means: Sarah. This is not an approach that moves from one place to another, nor a shift from one place to another. Rather, it is like someone saying, He came to curse me, meaning: He began to curse me. And his saying, in a shriek means: in a shout. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, in a bundle, meaning: in a shout.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then his wife came forward in a shriek and struck her face
. He means by the shriek: the shout.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In a bundle, he said: A shout.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So his wife came in a shriek
, meaning she came in a loud voice.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, a bundle, he said: It came ringing.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim Al-Yami, on the authority of Ibn Sabit,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then his wife came in a shriek
, he said: in a shout.

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then his wife came in a shriek
, he said: The shriek is the shout.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, in a bundle, meaning: a shout.

x: Some of them said that that shout is Oh, with the alif shortened. His saying,
h
So she slapped her face
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of she slapped her and the place on her face that she struck.
Some of them said: The meaning of she slapped her face is that he slapped her on it. Mention who said that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So she slapped her face
, meaning: she slapped him.

x: Others said: Rather, she hit her forehead with her hand in amazement.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me: Amr bin Hammad told us: Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When Gabriel gave Sarah the good report of Isaac and, after Isaac, Jacob, she struck her forehead in amazement. That is what He said:
h
So she struck her face

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
So she struck her face
, he said: her forehead.

c: Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim Al-Yami, on the authority of Ibn Sabit,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So she slapped her face
, he said: She said like this, and Sufyan hit his forehead with his hand. He said: Mahrān narrated to us on the authority of Sufyān,
h
So she slapped her face

, meaning she placed her hand on her forehead in amazement. To slap among the Arabs means to strike. It has been said that she slapped her face when she gathered her fingers and struck her forehead with them. And
h
a barren old woman

said, meaning: And she said: Will she give birth? And Will she give birth was omitted because the speech indicates it, and with the pronoun Will she give birth the word barren old woman was raised. What is meant by barren is the one who does not give birth.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sulayman Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Mishash:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
A barren old woman
, he said: She does not give birth.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us:
m: A man from Khorasan, from the Azd tribe, whose nickname was Abu Sasan, told us: I asked Al-Dahhak about his saying, barren. He said: The one who has no children.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Abraham’s guest said to his wife when she said to them, when they had given her the good report of a knowledgeable boy: Will you give birth to a barren old woman? They said: Thus says your Lord. He says: Thus says your Lord, meaning as We have informed you and said to you. He is the Wise, the Knowing. The ha in His statement
h
He is is from the mention of the Lord
, He is the Wise in His management of His creation, the Knowing of their interests and of what was and what will be.
And his saying, He said, ‘What is the matter with you, O messengers?’ He says: Abraham said to his guest: What is the matter with you, O messengers?
They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals.' They committed crimes because they disbelieved in God.
Let us send down upon them stones of clay. He says: Let us rain down upon them from the sky stones of clay marked, meaning: marked.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Marked with your Lord for the transgressors, he said: The marked stones are the sealed stones, the stone may be white with a black dot on it or the stone may be black with a white dot on it, so that is their marking with your Lord, O Abraham, for the transgressors, meaning for those who transgressed the limits of God, the disbelievers in Him from the people of Lot. Then We brought out whoever was therein of the believers, God Almighty says: So We brought out whoever was therein of the believers in God, they were Lot and his daughter, and He referred to the city by saying, whoever was therein, and it had not been mentioned before that.

x: God Almighty says: Marked by your Lord for the transgressors.
God Almighty says: Then We brought out whoever was in it of the believers.
God Almighty says: We did not find in that town from which we were expelled any believers in it except one house of Muslims, and that was the house of Lot.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And we did not find therein except one house of Muslims
, he said: If there had been more than that in it, God would have saved them so that they would know that faith is preserved with God and that its people are not lost.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said:
m: We did not find in it other than one house of Muslims. He said: These were the people of Lot. They did not find in it other than Lot.

c: Ibn Auf told me: Al-Mu'tamir told us: Safwan told us: Abu Al-Muthanna and Muslim Abu Al-Hail Al-Ashja'i told us:
m: God said, And We found therein no house except one of the Muslims, Lot and his two daughters. He said: The punishment befell them. God said, And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
b.via: Abu Al-Muthanna and Muslim Abu Al-Hail Al-Ashja'i

x: And His statement,
h
And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment

, means: And We left in this city from which We expelled those who were in it of the believers a sign. And the Most High said, And We left therein a sign, and the meaning is: And We left it as a sign because it was the one that was destroyed with its people, so it is the sign. And that is like the saying of the one who says: You see in this thing a lesson and a sign, and its meaning is: This thing is a sign and a warning, as the Most High said, Indeed in Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask Yusuf 7, and they were the signs and their actions, and what is meant by the sign is: the admonition and warning for those who fear the painful punishment of God in the Hereafter.

God Almighty says: And regarding Moses, son of Imran, when We sent him to Pharaoh with a proof that was clear to whoever saw it that it was a proof for Moses regarding the truth of what he was saying and calling for.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, to Pharaoh with clear authority, meaning: with a clear excuse.

x: And his saying,
h
So he turned away with his support

, means: So Pharaoh turned away, just as We sent Moses to him with his people, his soldiers and his companions. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, although the wording of those who said it differed. Mention who said that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So he turned away with his support
, meaning: to his people, or to his people. I am not sure.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
So he turned away with his support
, he said: with his arm and his companions.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
So he turned away with his support
, meaning the enemy of God defeated his people.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, the Most High,
h
So he turned away with his support

, he said: With his group that was with him. And he recited, If only I had against you strength or could take refuge in a strong support Hud 80. He said: To a force from among the people, to a support with which I could fight you. He said: And Pharaoh and his soldiers and those with him were his support. He said: And there was not with Lot a single believer. He said: And he offered them to marry his daughters in the hope that they would be a support to help him or defend him. And he recited, These are my daughters; they are purer for you Hud 78. He said: He meant marriage, but they refused. And he recited the statement of God, the Most High, Indeed, you know that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed, you know what we intend. Hud 79. The root of the word support is the side and direction that one relies on and is strengthened by. And his saying:
h
And a magician or a madman said

, meaning: And he said to Moses: He is a magician who bewitches people’s eyes or a madman who has a madness. And Muammar ibn al-Muthanna used to say: Or in this place means the waw of the conjunction because they had said both of them to him, and he recited in that regard the verse of Jarir al-Khatfi: Ath'alaba of the knights or winds that made them equal to Tahya and Al-Khashab

x: God Almighty says: “So We seized Pharaoh and his soldiers with anger and grief at Us. “So We cast them into the sea” meaning, “So We threw them into the sea and drowned them in it. “And he was blameworthy” meaning: Pharaoh was blameworthy, and the blameworthy is the one who committed the action for which he is blamed.
Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And he is blameworthy, meaning blameworthy in God’s blessings.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement, And He is blameworthy, he said: He is blameworthy regarding the servants of God. He mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw him away.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

evidence.text: He mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw him away.
